You are in charge of fixing a bug in the Go repository checked out at /gin (the gin-gonic/gin web framework). The user reported: "There is a bug in `errors.go`. Once it is fixed, the test `.::TestErrorUnwrap` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

Your job, end to end:
1. Read /gin/errors.go and /gin/errors_test.go carefully.
2. Run the existing test to see the current state: `cd /gin && go test -run 'TestError' -v ./... 2>&1 | head -60` (also try `go test -run TestErrorUnwrap -v .`). Record which tests fail BEFORE any edit (these are the pre-existing failures).
3. Find the root cause of why `TestErrorUnwrap` (behaviour: `errors.Is()` and `errors.As()` must work through a `*gin.Error` that wraps an inner error, including when wrapped again with `fmt.Errorf("%w", ...)`) fails. Inspect `git log -p -- errors.go` and `git diff` to see if a bug was introduced relative to the repository's own history (this is allowed: it is in-repo information).
4. Fix the bug with a MINIMAL edit to /gin/errors.go only (do not touch any test file, do not edit or delete pre-existing tests, do not add features).
5. Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test -run TestError -v .` and also run the full package test suite `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` to make sure no pre-existing passing test now fails. If a pre-existing test was already failing before your change, note it and leave it failing (do not fix it by editing tests).
6. Report back concisely: the exact root cause, the exact diff you applied (file + lines), the test commands you ran and their results (before and after), and whether the full test suite has any failures and whether they pre-existed.

Constraints: only modify /gin/errors.go. No new features. No test edits. No network access. Do not look at other installed copies of gin or the internet.
